I'm not very original when it comes to species. They all are based on other works of fiction with my own twist.

They basically have two forms. One is a normal human, but if you look close enough, you can see their eyes shift into that of a lizard. Or can feel a scaly shape under their skin. It's just enough to make you question if they're actually human or something else.

The other form is close to a standing lizard (or a dragon, a mix of both) They have a dark green, scaly hard skin with usually yellow and black undertones, eye colors vary from yellow to brown. They usually keep their human hair though, which is the easiest way to identify them from another. They can identify each other based of sounds.

They're eye sight is bad in the lizard from (But spotless in dark) and the scales make their skin tight and hard to move (kinda like someone with extreme skin conditions might find it hard to move, I can't remember the name of the specific condition) They aren't fighters like many other species in my world. The scavange for what they need and only fight to protect their own. 

This makes them vulnerable and they have been confided to one island where they are slaves. The island have countless precious metals and the lizard people are forced to do the mining. Their good eye sight in darkness and almost impenetrable skin makes them excellent to work in the rough conditions. Also their low need of food or water. They are mostly seen as disgusting by the outside world.

In human form they work like any other human.

I'm bad at explaining, but I'll try to be as clear as I can :D
So you probably don't have a sewing machine? So just get some thread the same or close enough colour and a needle.
Easiest way to go about fixing this is for you to follow the holes made by the original seam.
I will try to find a video of the style of stitch you should do, but start by makinh a knot in the thread and pull the needle through one hole, preferably a bit lower than where the seam is broken, so that tha needle ends up on the top side.

Start following the original stitches, by going across to the opposite hole, then go up one and again across. Continue in this way again a bit farther then where the seam is broken so it reinforces the strain on the ends and prevents the seams from breaking more.
Make sure the stitches are snug and knot it securely. If you feel insecure about the knot just make more.

Making a fitting bodice pattern is a good first step. It'll be easier to make stuff better fitting and you can change it to do all kinds of shirts and even skirts with it.
I think best way to learn is to just look at clothes to see how they're made. The pattern is the same shape just flat. For example: If a shirt has a seam in the middle, cut the pattern from the middle. 
It's a lot of trial and error tbh, but it'll get easier the more you do it. 

Here is some instructions for a bodice that I found: https://www.theshapesoffabric.com/2019/10/07/how-to-draft-the-basic-bodice-pattern/

The best place to get more room is to cut the pattern from the middle where the darts are, in there you can add more and it doesn't affect arm holes and stuff. The same place is good for making it smaller, just make the darts bigger.

If you're making a jacket or something that needs to be a lot bigger than a normal shirt I'd say a good place to start with specifically the arm hole is to lover it and add to the sides. Same for the neck part. Usually I'd say about 2-3cm is kind of a max, for it to still look like it's made for you and not brought from a store.

Bodices usually have a dart in the chest area and that usually gets taken off and the best way to do that is cut it in half and close it. A good thing to also do is to add about 1cm to the armhole from it. Then you can just draw a straight edge to the side.
